description: Fictional low-stakes scenarios for collecting direct, reviewable choice evidence. These questions do not contain or imply facts about any owner.

questions.prompt: A draft is useful but has one calculation you have not checked. A colleague wants it within the hour. What would you most likely do?

options.label: Send it now and flag the unchecked calculation
Check the calculation before sending
Send only the checked sections and follow up later

questions.prompt: You have thirty minutes before a routine decision meeting. How would you most likely use the time?

options.label: Write a short decision brief with a recommendation
Review the source materials without drafting a recommendation
Use the meeting itself to explore the decision

questions.prompt: You need a moderately priced household item this week and several options look adequate. What would you most likely do?

options.label: Buy the familiar option immediately
Compare a short list on the features that matter
Research the category broadly before choosing

questions.prompt: Two similar products differ mainly in price and return policy. Which would you most likely choose?

options.label: The cheapest option with limited returns
The slightly dearer option with easy returns
Delay the purchase until the difference is clearer

questions.prompt: An unexpectedly free Saturday appears. What would you most likely do first?

options.label: Make a short plan for the day
Start with whatever feels appealing
Keep the day deliberately unstructured for rest

questions.prompt: A small personal task is due in five days and will take about two hours. What would you most likely do?

options.label: Finish it in the next available block
Schedule a specific block closer to the deadline
Do a small part each day

questions.prompt: A small group is choosing between two harmless plans and you prefer the less popular one. What would you most likely do?

options.label: Explain your preference once, then accept the group decision
Defer to the group without arguing for your option
Propose a compromise or a way to try both

questions.prompt: You receive a pleasant invitation for an evening when you had planned quiet time alone. What would you most likely do?

options.label: Accept the invitation
Keep the quiet evening
Attend for a limited time

questions.prompt: You are planning a short leisure trip to a new city. Which approach would you most likely take?

options.label: Book a detailed itinerary in advance
Book a few anchors and leave the rest open
Keep almost everything spontaneous

questions.prompt: A low-stakes travel plan is disrupted and three acceptable alternatives are available. What would you most likely do first?

options.label: Choose the first workable alternative quickly
Compare the main trade-offs before choosing
Abandon the original aim and redesign the day

questions.prompt: A colleague asks for feedback on a draft with several fixable problems. How would you most likely respond?

options.label: Give a concise prioritized list of changes
Give detailed feedback with strengths and weaknesses
Ask questions that help them identify the changes

questions.prompt: You are asked for an answer based on incomplete but useful information. What would you most likely do?

options.label: Give the best current answer and state the uncertainty
Delay the answer until the key uncertainty is checked
Decline to answer without firmer evidence
